reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it directly promotes an automated Ethereum front-running bot as a source of passive income and unusually high profits, instructing viewers to deploy the contract and deposit Ethereum to its address. It presents reported returns of about 25% and three to five ETH over some weeks, while noting that gas and burn-fee risks exist and profits fluctuate. Those qualifications do not remove the connection between the promoted returns, required cryptocurrency funding, and bot workflow.

citations.quote: my bot which I call a front running bot allows you to automatically trade a given token from the ethereum blockchain without having to go through the typical manual transactional methods.

After the transaction is confirmed, it's your own BOT now 7. Deposit funds to your exact contract/bot address 8. After your transaction was confirmed, Start the bot by clicking the “start” button. Withdraw anytime by clicking the “withdrawal” button
which can help you make very easy daily passive income

You can fund the contract with however many Ethereum you want. But obviously, the more you put in, the larger the transactions you'll be able to front run and the more profit you'll be able to accumulate over time.
Well, guys, it's been a little over 24 hours, and now let's check the profits the bot worked for me. So now you can see I have around 1.26 ether, which is around 25% profit.

opening.argument: The presentation does not promise a fixed or guaranteed return. It expressly warns that insufficient funding can result in wasted gas fees, explains that burn fees vary, and states that profits fluctuate week to week. Those qualifications present the tool as a risky, conditional experiment whose outcome depends on network and token conditions, not as a certain way to make money. A report of personal results, even when optimistic, is not by itself proof that viewers are being deceived.

citations.quote: I have received messages from people who didn't fund the contract with enough Ethereum to cover gas fees and possible burn fees.
If you fund the contract with 0.4 ETH or less and the bot targets another token with high burn fees, the contract will basically waste a lot of gas fees.
the profits will fluctuate week to week

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited funding instructions show how to operate the software, but they do not establish a guaranteed return or concealment of risk. The reference side also omits the explicit warning that inadequate funding can waste gas and the statement that profits fluctuate. Even the reported result is framed as an observed personal result, not a promise that every viewer will obtain it.

citations.quote: the profits will fluctuate week to week
the contract will basically waste a lot of gas fees

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Risk language does not neutralize the solicitation. The video still calls the bot a way to make easy daily passive income and directs viewers to deposit funds into the contract. Saying results fluctuate qualifies the amount of return, but it does not withdraw the central income claim or prove that the demonstrated mechanism works.

Deposit funds to your exact contract/bot address

opening.argument: The central activity is an operational technology tutorial: creating a Solidity file, compiling it in Remix, deploying it through an injected Web3 environment, and using the resulting contract controls. The video explains what the buttons do and demonstrates the workflow on screen. Describing a personal run and its results is consistent with a software demonstration or technical walkthrough; it does not alone establish that the presentation is a deceptive solicitation. The audience is shown a reproducible process rather than merely being asked to trust an unexplained claim.

citations.quote: it's built with the 0.6.6 version of Solidity
now we have the deployment utility right here. now click the deploy button.
The start button will enable the bot to begin sniffing the meme pool. Withdraw will stop the bot and transfer funds back to your wallet.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side treats the presence of funding steps as proof of promotional intent, but technical tutorials necessarily explain deployment and operation. The cited phrases describe the bot's claimed function and the procedure; they do not establish that the demonstration is fabricated, that the code is malicious, or that viewers are guaranteed a return. A screen-recorded walkthrough remains evidence of instructional format.

citations.quote: So now we're going to deploy this to our wallet.
The start button will enable the bot to begin sniffing the meme pool.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The workflow is not presented as neutral programming instruction. It is paired with claims of easy passive income, directions to fund the deployed contract, and a reported 25% profit. Showing code and interface clicks demonstrates only that a workflow was shown; it does not establish that the bot generates the claimed profits or that depositing funds is safe.

citations.quote: which can help you make very easy daily passive income
Deposit funds to your exact contract/bot address
which is around 25% profit

opening.argument: At most, the material promotes a software tool and provides operational access points for using it. The supplied evidence does not show a request for passwords, seed phrases, identity documents, or account credentials, nor does it describe recruiting a downline or paying a membership fee. The instructions describe deployment, transaction fees, funding, starting, and withdrawing; they do not prove that the creator takes custody of the viewer's wallet or that a promised return is contractually guaranteed. That leaves substantial uncertainty about the alleged scam mechanism.

citations.quote: Access Remix Compiler
select injected web3 as the environment
Withdraw anytime by clicking the “withdrawal” button
we need to confirm creation of our contract by paying some gas fees

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side identifies a deposit and an income claim, but those facts alone do not prove that the creator receives the funds or that the contract cannot be withdrawn from. The cited instructions expressly describe deployment through the viewer's wallet and a withdrawal control. The record also lacks evidence of credential theft, recruitment, or a guaranteed contractual payout.

citations.quote: MetaMask will be connected to Remix
Withdraw will stop the bot and transfer funds back to your wallet.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing credential or downline elements are irrelevant because the asserted mechanism is funded-contract returns. The material explicitly tells viewers to deposit Ethereum to the contract, says larger deposits enable larger purported profits, and reports a 25% gain. A withdrawal button and wallet connection do not prove that the contract will actually return funds or produce the advertised income.
